question: A communications officer needs a one-page summary to hand out at an event, with the supporting detail available for anyone who asks afterwards. How should she organise the material?
options: A) Produce one long document containing both the summary and every piece of supporting detail.
B) Produce the handout only, and answer any requests for supporting detail verbally on the day.
C) Produce a short handout as the deliverable and keep the detail as a separate reference document.
D) Produce the supporting detail only, since anyone wanting a summary can read its opening section.
correct_answers: C) Produce a short handout as the deliverable and keep the detail as a separate reference document.
explanations: Incorrect. A single document that tries to do both is too long to hand out and too summary-led to serve as a reference.
Incorrect. Relying on recall leaves the detail unavailable afterwards and inconsistent between conversations.
Correct. Two audiences with different needs are served by two artefacts, so neither the handout nor the reference is compromised to accommodate the other.
Incorrect. An opening section written for a detailed document is not a handout, and event audiences will not read the rest.
